frontMatter.introduction:
RS Composite is a leading manufacturer in the textile and ready-made garments (RMG) industry, specializing in high-quality knitwear for global apparel brands. With extensive experience in garment manufacturing, fabric processing, printing, and finishing, RS Composite is committed to product quality, responsible production, worker welfare, and environmentally conscious operations across its manufacturing facilities.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual has been developed to ensure that all operational activities across the organization are carried out in a consistent, safe, and efficient manner, while meeting applicable legal, customer, and regulatory requirements. The manual establishes a unified operational framework that supports RS Composite's manufacturing processes from material sourcing and production planning to stitching, finishing, quality control, packing, and dispatch while reinforcing compliance with occupational health and safety, environmental management, and social responsibility standards relevant to the textile and apparel sector.

The SOP Manual serves as a comprehensive reference for employees, supervisors, managers, and technical personnel by clearly defining roles, responsibilities, and standardized work practices. It promotes operational discipline, ethical conduct, product consistency, and continuous improvement, thereby strengthening RS Composite's commitment to responsible manufacturing, workplace safety, and long-term sustainability across all its operations.
frontMatter.objective:
The primary objective of this SOP Manual is to:
Establish uniform and standardized procedures across all functional areas of RS Composite operations.
Ensure full compliance with applicable national labor laws, buyer codes of conduct, and relevant international standards applicable to the textile and ready-made garments (RMG) industry, including occupational health and safety, environmental management, chemical handling, and social compliance requirements.
Minimize process variability while enhancing product quality, workplace safety, operational reliability, and manufacturing efficiency.
Provide clear and structured guidance to employees at all levels to ensure consistent, accurate, and accountable execution of roles and responsibilities.
Serve as a reference document for internal audits, third-party social and quality audits, customer assessments, regulatory inspections, and ongoing employee training and capacity-building initiatives.

frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
The SOP Manual at RS Composite is reviewed on a structured and periodic basis to ensure its continued relevance, effectiveness, and compliance with applicable Bangladesh labor laws, corporate regulations, and industry best practices. This review mechanism supports operational consistency, risk management, and continuous improvement across all functions.

An annual comprehensive review of the SOP Manual is conducted.
Additional reviews are initiated following significant organizational, regulatory, technological, or operational changes.
Review triggers include:
Amendments to Bangladesh labor or corporate laws
Changes in regulatory expectations or compliance frameworks
Cybersecurity or data protection risks
Organizational restructuring or process changes
Updates to ISO certifications or management systems

Review Leads:
HR Manager – Human resources, labor practices, and workplace conduct SOPs
IT / Systems Manager – IT operations, data security, and cybersecurity-related SOPs
Operations Manager – Production processes, operational controls, and efficiency-related SOPs

Additional Stakeholders:
Senior Leadership
Compliance and Risk Management Representatives
Department Heads (as applicable)
External consultants or advisors for regulatory and technical guidance, where required

The SOP review process aims to:
Evaluate the effectiveness, clarity, and applicability of existing SOPs
Identify and remove outdated or redundant procedures
Integrate employee feedback and operational insights
Ensure ongoing compliance with the Bangladesh Labour Act, BIDA guidelines, and applicable industry standards
Strengthen governance, risk control, and operational alignment

Step 1 – Review Notification
The HR Department issues a formal review notification to relevant stakeholders at least one month in advance.

Step 2 – Review Meetings
Designated stakeholders review existing SOPs, assess gaps, and propose updates or improvements.

Step 3 – Feedback Integration
Employee and departmental feedback is documented, evaluated, and incorporated where relevant.

Step 4 – SOP Updates
Approved revisions are formally documented and integrated into the SOP Manual with version control.

Step 5 – Communication and Training
Updated SOPs are communicated through internal channels, including email and intranet, and training is conducted where required.

All SOP changes are recorded with revision summaries, dates, and justification notes.
The updated SOP Manual receives final approval from the Head of HR before release.

The latest approved SOP Manual is:
Available digitally on the company intranet or shared drive
Maintained in physical copies at relevant departmental offices for reference

By implementing a structured and periodic SOP review mechanism, RS Composite ensures that its procedures remain effective, compliant, and aligned with Bangladesh legal requirements, operational needs, and ethical business practices.

RS Composite is committed to reducing its environmental footprint across all stages of textile and ready-made garment manufacturing through a structured, practical, and compliant approach to resource use and waste management. As a knitwear manufacturer serving global apparel markets, RS Composite generates multiple waste streams including fabric off-cuts, yarn waste, rejected garments, packaging materials, chemical containers, sludge from effluent treatment, and general solid waste which require systematic and responsible handling.

This Waste Management Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes RS Composite's framework for the identification, segregation, storage, reuse, recycling, treatment, and disposal of waste generated from knitting, cutting, stitching, printing, finishing, washing, packing, utilities, warehouses, and administrative areas. The SOP integrates principles of waste minimization, resource efficiency, circular economy, and regulatory compliance, ensuring that environmental responsibility remains embedded in day-to-day manufacturing operations. It supports pollution prevention, continual improvement, and alignment with internationally recognised environmental management practices, including ISO 14001 and responsible sourcing expectations of global apparel brands.
The objectives of this Waste Management SOP are to:

Minimise material consumption and waste generation through efficient production planning, cutting optimisation, defect reduction, and process control.
Identify, segregate, collect, store, transport, and dispose of all waste streams in accordance with applicable environmental regulations and local authority requirements in Bangladesh, as well as international buyer expectations.
Promote circular resource practices, including fabric recycling, yarn recovery, reuse of packaging materials, safe recycling of chemical containers, and responsible handling of effluent treatment plant (ETP) waste.
Ensure clear accountability of employees, supervisors, contractors, and waste handlers in implementing environmentally responsible waste management practices.
Support effective implementation of the Environmental Management System (EMS) and reinforce RS Composite's broader sustainability and ESG commitments.
This Waste Management SOP applies to:

All departments within RS Composite, including knitting, cutting, stitching, printing, embroidery, washing, finishing, quality control, quality assurance, production planning, industrial engineering, utilities, engineering and maintenance, warehousing, packing, administration, human resources, and sustainability functions.
All categories of waste generated across operations, including but not limited to solid waste, liquid waste, hazardous and non-hazardous waste, chemical waste, sludge from effluent treatment plants (ETP), fabric and yarn waste, packaging waste, recyclable materials, and electronic waste (e-waste).
All personnel involved in material handling and waste-related activities, including employees, supervisors, contract workers, housekeeping staff, waste handlers, and third-party service providers responsible for segregation, storage, transport, recycling, treatment, or disposal of waste.
All RS Composite operational locations, including manufacturing facilities, production floors, utility areas, chemical storage rooms, effluent treatment facilities, warehouses, packing areas, and administrative offices, ensuring consistent implementation of waste management practices across the organization.

body.text: RS Composite enforces strict waste segregation at the point of generation to prevent contamination, improve recyclability, and ensure compliance with applicable environmental regulations and buyer expectations within the textile and ready-made garments (RMG) sector.
Color-Coded Bin System (Standardized Across All Facilities)

Red Bin – Hazardous waste (chemical-contaminated rags, sludge from printing/washing, contaminated containers, oily waste).
Blue Bin – Recyclable waste (clean plastic bottles, polybags, polyethylene films, cartons, paper, glass, metal scrap).
Yellow Bin – Contaminated PPE and cleaning materials (chemical-contaminated gloves, absorbents, wipes).
Green Bin – Organic waste (canteen food waste and biodegradable waste).
All bins are clearly labelled in English and the local language, supported by visual signage and icons to ensure easy identification by all employees and contract workers.
Staff Training & Awareness

Mandatory waste segregation and environmental awareness training is conducted at least once every six months for employees, contract workers, housekeeping staff, and facility personnel.
Training includes practical demonstrations, visual posters, on-floor guidance, and toolbox talks.
All new employees receive waste segregation and environmental awareness training as part of their onboarding process.
Refresher sessions are conducted periodically through departmental meetings and internal communication channels.
Bin Maintenance & Monitoring

Waste bins are inspected and cleaned daily by housekeeping supervisors.
Waste transfer is carried out using designated, colour-coded trolleys to prevent cross-contamination.
Damaged, overflowing, or incorrectly labelled bins are immediately replaced or corrected.
Supervisors and the EHS team conduct routine checks to ensure segregation compliance at the point of generation.

RS Composite recognises the potential environmental, health, and safety risks associated with hazardous waste generated during textile and ready-made garment (RMG) manufacturing activities. Hazardous waste at RS Composite may arise from processes such as printing, washing, dyeing support activities, chemical handling, effluent treatment operations, maintenance work, and utility functions. Typical hazardous wastes include chemical-contaminated sludge, used oils and lubricants, contaminated containers, oily rags, chemical residues, and contaminated personal protective equipment (PPE).

This Hazardous Waste Management Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes a structured and comprehensive framework for the identification, segregation, handling, storage, internal movement, transportation, and final disposal of hazardous waste generated across all RS Composite facilities. The SOP is designed to prevent environmental pollution, reduce occupational health and safety risks, ensure legal compliance, and protect employees, contractors, surrounding communities, and the environment.

Aligned with applicable environmental regulations in Bangladesh, recognised international environmental management practices, and the principles of ISO 14001, this SOP ensures that hazardous waste is managed in a manner that:

Minimises environmental impact and pollution risks
Promotes safe handling and controlled disposal
Upholds employee health, safety, and well-being
Supports RS Composite’s sustainability and ESG commitments
The primary objectives of this Hazardous Waste Management SOP are to:

Ensure safe, compliant, and traceable handling of all hazardous waste generated at RS Composite facilities.
Establish clear procedures for identification, labelling, containment, and storage of hazardous waste streams.
Reduce hazardous waste generation through process optimisation, efficient chemical usage, preventive maintenance, and material substitution where feasible.
Define clear roles and responsibilities for hazardous waste handling, internal transfer, and final disposal.
Support compliance with national environmental regulations, buyer environmental requirements, and environmental management system principles aligned with ISO 14001.
This SOP applies to:

All functional departments involved in the generation, storage, or handling of hazardous waste, including but not limited to:
Printing, Washing, and Finishing Operations
Chemical Storage and Handling Areas
Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and Utilities
Engineering and Maintenance
Production Floors and Support Areas
Quality Control and Inspection Areas
Warehouse, Raw Material, and Finished Goods Stores
EHS, Compliance, and Sustainability Functions

Printing and washing sludge

Used oils, lubricants, and grease
Chemical-contaminated containers, drums, and packaging

Flammable, corrosive, or toxic chemical wastes

Permanent employees

Third-party logistics providers and authorised waste disposal vendors

blocks.text: RS Composite actively integrates circular economy principles and safer chemical management practices into its hazardous waste management framework. The focus is on reducing hazardous waste at source, improving material efficiency, recovering usable inputs, and transitioning to less hazardous and more sustainable alternatives wherever technically and commercially feasible within the textile and RMG industry.

body.text:
Chemical Reuse & Recovery in Printing and Washing Operations:
Reuse of Cleaning Solutions:
Recovery of Packaging Inputs:
ETP By-product Management:
Side Stream Utilization:

Residual chemicals from printing pastes, washing auxiliaries, and finishing processes are assessed for reuse where feasible. Controlled reuse of low-risk chemicals is carried out after internal verification to reduce fresh chemical consumption and waste generation.

Cleaning solutions used for equipment, screens, and tools are segregated by type and contamination level. Where quality and safety parameters allow, these solutions are reused for non-critical cleaning or pre-cleaning activities.

Chemical drums, containers, and IBCs are cleaned and reused internally where permitted or returned to suppliers undertake-back arrangements, reducing hazardous container waste.

Sludge and residues generated from effluent treatment are monitored for calorific value and disposal suitability. Where permitted, co-processing or authorized treatment routes are explored to minimize landfill disposal.

Wash water or rinse streams with acceptable quality parameters are reused for secondary washing, floor cleaning, or utility purposes, subject to internal controls and regulatory allowances.

Periodic reviews are conducted to identify opportunities to replace hazardous chemicals used in printing, washing, and finishing with lower-toxicity or environmentally preferable alternatives.

Preference is given to water-based inks, dyes, and auxiliaries, as well as low volatile organic compound (VOC) formulations, to reduce air emissions and health risks.

Where feasible, bio-based softeners, enzyme-based detergents, and biodegradable auxiliaries are adopted to reduce chemical load in effluents and hazardous waste streams.

Phosphate-free detergents and eco-labelled cleaning agents are used in washing, housekeeping, and equipment cleaning to minimize aquatic toxicity.

Maintenance workshops use water-based degreasers for machinery and component cleaning, reducing reliance on petroleum-based solvents.

Preference is given to suppliers providing chemicals in recyclable, reusable, or returnable packaging such as reusable drums and IBCs, with minimal secondary packaging.

steps.heading: Use of Alternative and Less Hazardous Substances

body.text:
High-hazard chemicals used in printing, washing, and finishing are systematically reviewed and replaced with safer alternatives where process performance and product quality are not compromised.

Chemicals classified as carcinogenic, mutagenic, reprotoxic, or highly sensitizing are avoided wherever possible, and use is restricted only to essential applications with strict controls.

Substances restricted under international apparel standards and buyer RSL/MRSL requirements are phased out, with strong monitoring of incoming chemicals.

Strong acids and alkalis are replaced with milder formulations in cleaning and finishing processes where feasible, reducing corrosion risks and hazardous effluent loads.

The Procurement team follows a substitution-first approach, prioritising suppliers offering safer, environmentally responsible chemical alternatives that meet performance and compliance requirements.

Chemical sourcing decisions consider hazard classification, environmental fate, and lifecycle impacts, particularly for high-volume printing and washing chemicals.

Supplier evaluations include environmental and safety criteria such as reduction of hazardous content, waste minimization initiatives, packaging take-back programs, and regulatory compliance.

RS Composite builds long-term partnerships with suppliers demonstrating strong sustainability credentials, transparent chemical disclosure, and alignment with responsible manufacturing practices.

blocks.text: Proper identification, secure containment, and compliant movement of hazardous waste are critical to minimising risks related to chemical exposure, spills, fire hazards, environmental damage, and regulatory non-compliance. RS Composite has established detailed and rigorous protocols for hazardous waste labelling, storage, handling, and transportation, aligned with applicable Bangladesh environmental regulations, recognised international chemical safety practices, and buyer environmental compliance expectations. These protocols ensure full operational control, traceability, and accountability throughout the hazardous waste lifecycle.

body.text:
Each hazardous waste container whether drum, barrel, carboy, IBC, or bag—is labelled immediately at the point of generation and remains fully traceable until final treatment or disposal.

Labelling Standards

All hazardous waste containers must be labelled in accordance with the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) and applicable national standards. Labels must be:

Clearly printed, laminated, and weather-resistant
Firmly affixed to the container
Easily visible from all accessible sides

Label Requirements

Each label must include the following information:

Material / Waste Stream Name (e.g., Printing Sludge, Washing Chemical Residue, Used Oil, ETP Sludge)
Chemical Composition / Primary Hazardous Constituents (where applicable)
Physical State (solid / liquid / sludge)
GHS Hazard Class Symbols (flammable, corrosive, toxic, reactive, etc.)
Generating Department & Responsible Contact Person
Accumulation Start Date & Maximum Storage Duration (as per regulatory limits)
Waste Quantity (gross, net, and container weight where applicable)
Proposed Disposal Method (authorised recycler, incineration, secure landfill, co-processing)
Container Identification Number / Barcode

Label Implementation Notes

All labels are bilingual (English and local language) to ensure universal understanding.
Barcodes or unique container numbers are logged into the Hazardous Waste Tracking Register or equivalent system maintained by the EHS team.
Internal colour-coded label borders are used as visual identification aids:
Red Border – Toxic or highly hazardous waste
Orange Border – Flammable waste
Yellow Border – Reactive or unstable waste
Black Border – Corrosive waste

In cases where containers are reused (e.g., cleaned chemical drums), all previous labels must be completely removed and destroyed before new labels are applied to prevent misidentification and accidental misuse.

Hazardous waste is stored only in designated, secured, and engineered storage areas designed to prevent leakage, incompatible mixing, fire risk, unauthorised access, and environmental exposure.

Physical Infrastructure Requirements

Chemical-resistant, epoxy-coated flooring to prevent seepage and allow easy cleaning.
Secondary containment systems, bund walls, or spill pallets with a minimum capacity of 110% of the largest container stored.
Fire detection systems, including smoke detectors and heat sensors, connected to the central fire alarm system.
Restricted access controls, allowing entry only to trained and authorised personnel.
Adequate ventilation to prevent accumulation of hazardous vapours.
Intrinsically safe, spark-proof lighting and electrical fittings in areas storing flammable waste.
Storage Management Controls

Hazardous wastes are segregated based on compatibility (e.g., acids separated from alkalis; flammables isolated from oxidisers).
Containers are kept sealed at all times except during waste addition or inspection.
Storage areas are clearly marked with hazard signage and emergency contact information.
Maximum storage duration limits are strictly monitored and documented by the EHS team.

Segregation Protocols

At RS Composite, hazardous waste is segregated based on chemical compatibility, physical properties, and risk profile to prevent reactions, fires, spills, and cross-contamination. Dedicated zones are clearly demarcated and controlled.

rows: Isolated cabinets or enclosures with mechanical ventilation, restricted access, and prominent hazard signage
Dedicated stainless-steel shelving with yellow floor and shelf markings and clear “Oxidizer” signage
Flame-proof storage cabinets or rooms with proper earthing and bonding provisions
Bunded sections with warning tape, secondary containment, and specific hazard labels
Physically segregated areas with barriers and clear incompatibility signage

body.text: Operational Practices

Hazardous waste containers are stored above ground level on polymer or chemical-resistant pallets to prevent corrosion and contact with floor spillages.
FIFO (First In, First Out) principles are strictly followed. Accumulation start dates are clearly mentioned to ensure waste is not stored beyond permitted time limits.
Daily inspections are conducted and documented by authorised personnel to check for:
Leaks, corrosion, bulging, or deterioration of containers
Integrity, accuracy, and readability of labels
Housekeeping standards and pest control status
Direction arrows, storage area layouts, emergency contact details, and GHS hazard signage are prominently displayed throughout hazardous waste storage and movement zones.

To prevent chemical burns, inhalation exposure, fire or reactivity incidents, and ergonomic injuries, RS Composite enforces strict handling procedures for all hazardous waste–related activities.

Personnel Qualification

Only trained and authorised personnel are permitted to handle hazardous waste containers.
Training covers:
Correct PPE selection, use, and limitations
Chemical compatibility, segregation rules, and incompatibility risks
Emergency spill response and use of spill kits
Fire safety measures, extinguisher use, and evacuation procedures
PPE Requirements by Waste Type

rows: Antistatic gloves, chemical splash goggles, FFP2 mask or equivalent, chemical-resistant apron, ESD safety shoes
Acid-resistant gloves, full face shield, chemical splash suit or apron, gumboots
Flame-retardant coverall, appropriate respirator, nitrile gloves, use of local exhaust ventilation or hood where required

body.text: Material Handling Tools

Dedicated trolleys with secondary containment trays for safe movement of drums and containers.
Drum lifters, grabbers, or rotators for handling large containers; manual lifting of full drums is strictly prohibited.
Spill-resistant pumps or closed transfer systems for liquid movement; manual tipping or pouring is not permitted.

Transportation of hazardous waste, both within RS Composite premises and to authorised off-site facilities, is carried out with maximum safety and regulatory control.

Internal Transfer (Within Premises)

Only approved, corrosion-resistant, and antistatic trolleys are used on designated routes.
Containers are:
Properly sealed and secured with lid locks or restraints
Covered where there is potential for vapour release or odour
Movement is preferably planned during non-peak production hours to minimise interaction with routine operations.
Routes are pre-mapped, clearly marked, and kept free from obstructions.
External Transfer (To Authorised Treatment / Disposal Facilities)

Only government-authorised transporters and vehicles are engaged.
The EHS team prepares and verifies required waste manifests and transport documentation in line with regulatory and buyer requirements.
Containers are loaded on:
Covered vehicles with appropriate hazard placards
UN-approved sealed containers where applicable
Vehicles equipped with spill kits, MSDS folders, and emergency contact information
Disposal receipts and weight reconciliation slips are obtained and recorded in the EHS compliance system within defined timelines.
All vehicles used for hazardous waste transport must:

Be fitted with ABC-type fire extinguishers accessible to the driver and loading area.
Carry spill containment kits appropriate to the waste type.
Provide adequate ventilation to prevent vapour accumulation.
Use GPS-based tracking systems, where applicable, to enable monitoring of route adherence and transport status.
In the event of an accident, spill, leakage, fire, or any transport-related emergency involving hazardous waste:

The Transport Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is immediately activated by the transport team and EHS.
Primary actions include:
Securing the area and restricting unauthorised access
Eliminating ignition sources and stopping vehicle engines were safe
Deploying spill kits to contain or neutralise the release
Using appropriate PPE based on the hazard class involved
Secondary actions include:
Informing local emergency services, authorities, and medical facilities as required
Notifying the EHS Head and Site Incident Controller
Initiating internal incident reporting procedures
Following stabilisation, a detailed Root Cause Analysis (RCA) is conducted. Findings and corrective actions are recorded, and CAPA measures are implemented to prevent recurrence.

All hazardous waste transport activities form part of RS Composite’s compliance and audit trail.

Transport records capture:

Transporter name, licence details, and vehicle registration
Driver details and contact information
Route and key checkpoints
Date and time of departure and arrival
Container identification numbers, waste categories, and quantities
Records are retained for a minimum of five years, or longer where required by regulations, buyer requirements, or RS Composite’s internal data-retention policy.

A Material Movement Register (MMR) is maintained for every internal movement of hazardous waste.
Records include container ID, waste type, quantity, source department, destination, handler name, PPE confirmation, and time/date of movement.

sections.title: Specialized Treatment & Safe Disposal of Hazardous Substances

body.text:
To minimise environmental impact and reduce dependency on external disposal facilities, RS Composite implements multiple in-plant pre-treatment measures before hazardous waste is sent off-site:

pH Neutralisation Systems

Installed in printing, washing, utilities, and maintenance wash areas.
Treat acidic and alkaline wastewater generated during equipment cleaning and process washdowns.
Equipped with automated pH monitoring and controlled dosing systems to bring wastewater within acceptable limits before routing to the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP).

Oil & Chemical Separation Units

Used oils, greases, and oily wastewater from maintenance activities pass through oil–water separators to isolate hydrocarbons prior to further treatment or disposal.

Filtration & Adsorption Systems

Activated carbon and filtration units are used at selected discharge points to remove colour, residual chemicals, surfactants, and trace contaminants from wash water prior to ETP/STP treatment.

All hazardous waste that cannot be safely reused, recycled, or treated on-site is transferred only to government-authorised hazardous waste treatment and disposal facilities, in line with Bangladesh environmental regulations and buyer expectations.

Treatment, Storage & Disposal Facilities (TSDF / Authorized Facilities)

Non-recoverable hazardous waste streams include:

Printing and washing sludge
ETP sludge
Spent activated carbon and filter media
Used oils and contaminated absorbents
Chemical-contaminated packaging and PPE

High-Temperature Incineration

Used for high-calorific and toxic wastes such as contaminated rags, absorbents, oily residues, and chemical sludge, ensuring destruction of hazardous constituents.

Secure Engineered Landfilling

Used for inorganic, non-recyclable hazardous solids, including filter cakes, ash, and stabilised residues, with engineered liners and leachate control systems.

Pre-Dispatch Controls

Before dispatch to authorised facilities:

Waste is fully segregated by category
Containers are sealed, labelled, and documented
Waste characteristics (where required) are reviewed to determine the appropriate treatment route

RS Composite adopts multiple source-level and system-level strategies to minimise hazardous emissions and reduce downstream treatment loads:

Process Parameter Optimisation

Printing, washing, and finishing parameters (chemical dosage, temperature, dwell time, liquor ratios) are optimised to reduce chemical losses and hazardous residues.

In-Process Recycling & Reuse

Controlled reuse of wash water, low-risk chemical streams, and internal recycling initiatives are implemented where validated and permitted.

Standardised Operating Protocols

Detailed SOPs govern chemical addition, concentration limits, storage, and usage to prevent overdosing, spills, and unintended reactions.

narrative.text:
Monitoring of pH, temperature, flow rates, and chemical usage at critical points enables early intervention and prevents off-spec emissions.

Targeted Contaminant Isolation

Filtration, sedimentation, and phase separation techniques are used to isolate hazardous constituents before they enter bulk effluent streams.

Onsite Hazard Reduction

Neutralisation, dilution, or controlled treatment is applied at source to reduce hazard classification before final disposal.

RS Composite recognises water as a critical and finite resource that underpins its textile and ready-made garment (RMG) manufacturing operations, including knitting, cutting, stitching, printing, washing, finishing, utilities, and domestic use. As a garment manufacturer supplying global markets, responsible water stewardship is central to RS Composite’s sustainability strategy, regulatory compliance, buyer expectations, and long-term operational resilience.

This Integrated Water Management SOP defines RS Composite’s structured and comprehensive approach to water abstraction, consumption, quality monitoring, conservation, treatment, reuse, and wastewater discharge. It addresses operational and environmental risks associated with water use, including risks related to dyes, auxiliaries, surfactants, oils, suspended solids, and other textile-processing contaminants present in wastewater streams. The SOP ensures that water management is proactive, preventive, and aligned with responsible manufacturing and environmental protection principles.
The objectives of this Integrated Water Management SOP are to:

Ensure efficient, controlled, and minimised use of water across all operational areas, including production floors, printing and washing units, utilities, laboratories (where applicable), and domestic services.
Monitor, analyse, and manage wastewater responsibly through in-house Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) systems, and through authorised external discharge arrangements where applicable.
Implement source-level controls to capture, isolate, and reduce contaminants such as dyes, chemicals, oils, and suspended solids before they enter common effluent streams.
Integrate routine water audits, metered consumption tracking, and water quality monitoring into operational controls, management reviews, and sustainability reporting frameworks.
Ensure compliance with applicable local and national water regulations, environmental discharge standards, buyer requirements, and international sustainability expectations relevant to the textile and apparel industry.
This SOP applies to all departments and activities that consume water or generate wastewater, including but not limited to:

Production Operations (knitting, cutting, stitching support activities)
Printing, Washing, and Finishing Units
Quality Control and Inspection Areas
Utilities and HVAC Systems (boilers, cooling towers, chillers, air washers, compressors)
Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and Sewage Treatment Plant (STP)
Maintenance, equipment cleaning, and floor washing operations
Sanitary and domestic uses (canteen, washrooms, housekeeping, drinking water systems)

responsibilities: Ensure effective implementation of this SOP across all RS Composite facilities; conduct employee and contractor training; perform internal audits; monitor compliance; and prepare reports related to water use, wastewater treatment, reuse, and regulatory adherence.

Monitor water consumption within knitting, cutting, stitching, printing, washing, and finishing areas; ensure local conservation measures and SOP controls are followed; identify inefficiencies; and promptly report deviations or abnormal usage trends to EHS and Utilities teams.

Maintain plumbing systems, pipelines, pumps, valves, cooling towers, boilers, RO plants, STP and ETP units; conduct leak detection and repairs; and perform routine inspections to ensure uninterrupted and efficient water management infrastructure.

Source and procure water-efficient fixtures (low-flow taps, aerators), efficient valves and fittings, metering devices, RO membranes, treatment chemicals, and consumables required for water treatment and conservation initiatives.

Use water responsibly during operations and domestic use; promptly report leaks, overflows, or abnormal consumption; comply with department-specific water usage guidelines; and actively participate in water conservation awareness programmes.

blocks.text:
Water used in printing, washing, finishing, quality testing, and supporting production activities is metered at department or process level wherever feasible to enable consumption tracking and optimisation.
Reverse Osmosis (RO) systems used for process and utility water are operated to maximise recovery rates and minimise reject water generation, supported by preventive maintenance and membrane health monitoring.
Equipment, screen, and floor cleaning procedures are designed using defined water quantities or validated cleaning cycles, avoiding uncontrolled free-flow washing and unnecessary water losses.

body.text: Regular preventive maintenance is carried out on cooling towers, chillers, condensers, air washers, and heat exchangers to ensure optimal thermal performance, minimise water loss due to leaks or drift, and maintain energy efficiency.

steps.heading: Leak Monitoring and Immediate Repair Protocol

body.text: Moisture sensors, level indicators, and routine visual inspections are used to detect leaks in cooling and utility water circuits. Identified leaks are logged and rectified within 24 hours to prevent water wastage and operational disruption.

Where technically and economically feasible, RS Composite operates closed-loop cooling systems for chillers and process equipment, reducing blowdown losses, preventing contamination, and minimising wastewater discharge from cooling operations.

Cooling intensity is automatically adjusted based on real-time production load, ambient conditions, and machine requirements through control systems, preventing overcooling and unnecessary water and energy consumption.

Water-efficient alternatives such as air-cooled chillers, hybrid cooling systems, drift eliminators, and high-efficiency tower internals are implemented or evaluated to reduce reliance on water-intensive cooling methods.

Technologies such as Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs), improved insulation, condensate recovery, and optimised pump operations are used to simultaneously reduce water abstraction and electricity consumption.

Daily and monthly logs covering make-up water usage, blowdown volumes, cycles of concentration, and energy consumption are maintained to identify inefficiencies and support continuous improvement initiatives.

Pre-treatment of process wastewater from printing and washing operations is carried out using:
Activated carbon filters for colour and organic load reduction
pH neutralisation tanks to correct acidic or alkaline streams
Chemical-laden liquid waste (e.g., high-strength printing residues, oils, solvents used in maintenance) is segregated at source, stored in labelled containers, and handed over to authorised hazardous waste handlers instead of being mixed with general effluent.
All industrial wastewater is routed to the in-house Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and domestic wastewater to the Sewage Treatment Plant (STP), where appropriate physical, chemical, and biological treatment processes are employed to reduce pollutants.
Where applicable, treated effluent meeting prescribed standards is discharged to an authorised Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) or approved discharge points, ensuring compliance with regulatory norms.
Greywater streams, including RO reject, cooling tower blowdown (where permissible), and wash water from handwash stations, are collected separately and reused for non-critical applications such as toilet flushing, floor cleaning, or gardening (where permitted).
RS Composite maintains formal agreements with authorised CETP operators and treatment partners, supported by periodic effluent sampling and testing through accredited laboratories to verify compliance.

No untreated or partially treated industrial or domestic wastewater is discharged to soil, open drains, or natural water bodies. This requirement is strictly enforced across all facilities.
Effluent is managed through closed collection systems and routed only to authorised treatment facilities (ETP/STP/CETP).
Secondary containment such as trays and drip pans are installed beneath chemical storage, printing chemical areas, fuel storage, and critical equipment.
Spill kits containing absorbents, neutralisers, and booms are positioned at strategic locations for immediate response.
Containment systems, bunds, trenches, and barriers are inspected periodically to ensure integrity.
Groundwater abstraction (where applicable) is monitored monthly, and groundwater levels and quality are reviewed annually through internal checks or third-party testing.

sections.title: Rainwater Harvesting and On-Site Water Reuse Initiative

blocks.text:
System Implementation

A dedicated rainwater harvesting system has been installed across suitable roof catchment areas of the facility. Rainwater is collected through a network of gutters and downpipes, passed through initial filtration units to remove debris and sediments, and directed into designated storage tanks.

The system has been designed considering local rainfall patterns, roof area availability, and on-site water demand to ensure effective capture and utilization.

Utilization of Harvested Rainwater

Collected rainwater is safely reused for non-potable applications within the facility, including:

Floor washing and general cleaning activities
Utility and housekeeping purposes
Gardening and greenbelt maintenance
Other approved operational uses where potable water quality is not required

This reuse directly reduces freshwater consumption from external sources and lowers operational water costs.

Monitoring and Performance Tracking

RS Composite maintains periodic records of harvested rainwater volumes and its end-use applications. Usage data is reviewed to assess system effectiveness and contribution to overall water reduction targets.

Seasonal comparisons are conducted to evaluate performance during monsoon and non-monsoon periods.

System Inspection and Maintenance

Regular inspections and preventive maintenance are carried out to ensure the system remains functional and efficient. Activities include:

Cleaning of gutters and filters
Inspection of storage tanks for leaks or contamination
Verification of water flow paths and drainage integrity

Maintenance and inspection records are documented to demonstrate system upkeep and long-term reliability.

Supporting Documentation Maintained

The following documents are available for verification and audit purposes:

Rainwater harvesting system installation report
Harvested rainwater use and monitoring reports
System inspection and maintenance logs

sections.title: Removal of Dyes, Chemicals, and Hazardous Textile Residues from Wastewater

blocks.text: RS Composite applies a multi-layered strategy to minimise and eliminate dyes, auxiliaries, surfactants, and other hazardous textile-processing residues from wastewater, preventing contamination of surface water, soil, and aquatic ecosystems.

sections.title: Removal of Dyes, Chemicals, and Hazardous Textile Residues from Wastewater

body.text:
High-strength streams containing dyes, pigments, chemicals, oils, or finishing auxiliaries—such as printing wash water, screen cleaning effluents, concentrated spill washings, and chemical mixing residues—are identified and segregated at the point of generation.
These streams are not discharged into stormwater drains or untreated biological systems.

Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) systems are used to remove colour, organic compounds, and residual chemicals from high-risk wastewater streams.
Multi-barrier polishing units, combining filtration, adsorption, and sedimentation, are evaluated or deployed to enhance final effluent quality prior to discharge or reuse.
Concentrated chemical- or dye-bearing wastewater and sludge are collected in leak-proof, labelled containers specifying:

Chemical or dye type
Approximate concentration
Volume
Generation source (process, department, batch reference)

Containers are tracked through internal registers to ensure full traceability.
Such waste is stored in designated hazardous areas and disposed of through authorised treatment and disposal facilities in compliance with environmental regulations.
RS Composite’s EHS and Engineering teams continuously evaluate advanced treatment options, including:

Enhanced biological treatment for improved degradation of textile organics
Advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) for colour and chemical breakdown
Improved adsorption media and filtration technologies
Collaborations with technology providers, laboratories, and industry experts are pursued to assess scalability, efficiency, and economic feasibility.

All wastewater management practices align with evolving national regulations and international benchmarks for textile wastewater, including buyer requirements and recognised industry guidance on colour, COD, heavy metals, and chemical residue control.

sections.title: Water Efficiency, Low-Impact Processing, and Responsible Washing Practices

blocks.text:
Context and Commitment

RS Composite is committed to minimizing freshwater consumption and reducing wastewater pollution arising from washing, cleaning, surface treatment, and finishing operations associated with composite manufacturing. As a Bangladesh-based facility operating in a water-stressed region, the company prioritizes water efficiency, chemical optimization, and pollution prevention as core environmental performance objectives.

This integrated approach focuses on reducing water use at source, improving washing efficiency, and limiting the discharge of high-impact chemicals, including those contributing to AOX in wastewater.

sections.title: Water Efficiency, Low-Impact Processing, and Responsible Washing Practices

body.text:
RS Composite has implemented optimized washing and cleaning practices to reduce excessive water consumption without compromising product quality or workplace hygiene. Traditional high-volume wash practices are replaced, where feasible, with controlled and efficient cleaning methods.
Key measures include the use of low-flow nozzles, pressure-assisted cleaning equipment, and optimized wash cycles that limit water use to only what is operationally necessary. Cleaning processes are standardized through defined work instructions to avoid prolonged or repeated washing.
Sequential washing practices are applied so that lightly contaminated rinse water may be reused for initial cleaning stages, reducing overall freshwater demand.

Washing processes are designed with defined parameters for time, pressure, temperature, and chemical concentration. Operators follow approved work instructions that prevent over-washing, uncontrolled hose use, or unnecessary re-cleaning.
Routine monitoring of water consumption helps identify deviations and improvement opportunities, while maintenance checks ensure that valves, hoses, and spray systems remain leak-free and efficient.

In parallel with water reduction initiatives, RS Composite actively works to minimize AOX load in wastewater by reducing the use of chlorine-based chemicals and sodium chlorate in surface treatment, bleaching, or cleaning-related applications.
Where technically feasible, alternative low-AOX or non-chlorinated chemicals are used. Chemical selection decisions prioritize environmental compatibility, lower toxicity, and reduced halogen content.
Controlled chemical dosing systems ensure accurate application, preventing excess chemical discharge during washing or cleaning stages.

Water-efficient machinery and fixtures are installed in relevant production and cleaning areas. These include controlled spray systems, recirculation-supported wash units, and equipment designed to deliver effective cleaning with reduced water volumes.
Installation records and equipment manuals are maintained to demonstrate correct setup, operation, and maintenance of water-saving systems.

RS Composite maintains operational efficiency reports tracking water consumption trends, washing process performance, and chemical usage. These records support internal reviews and provide documented evidence for audits and customer assessments.
Effluent parameters are periodically reviewed to assess the effectiveness of water-saving and low-AOX measures, ensuring alignment with regulatory limits and buyer expectations.
RS Composite ensures continuous improvement in water stewardship and wastewater management through:

Quarterly EHS reviews of water usage trends, leak reports, and reuse performance
Annual third-party audits of water systems and effluent quality
Regular evaluation of high-recovery RO systems, improved ETP performance, and advanced treatment technologies

Employee-driven initiatives Kaizen programmes, awareness training, and internal communication embed responsible water use into daily operations. Data from consumption logs, reuse metrics, leak repair records, and treatment performance is systematically analysed to guide targeted upgrades and long-term sustainability planning.

sops.title: Air Emissions Compliance and Community Impact Prevention

blocks.text: RS Composite recognises that maintaining clean air within and around its manufacturing facilities is a critical element of environmental stewardship, worker health and safety, and responsible community engagement. As a knitwear and ready-made garment (RMG) manufacturer, RS Composite operates a range of activities—including knitting, cutting, stitching, printing, washing, finishing, utilities, and material handling—that can generate air emissions such as dust, lint, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), chemical vapours, combustion gases, odours, and noise if not properly managed.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the preventive strategies, engineering controls, monitoring systems, and management practices adopted by RS Composite to control atmospheric emissions, process-generated vapours, workplace dust, odours, and noise. These measures are designed to ensure compliance with applicable environmental and occupational health regulations, meet international buyer expectations, and protect employees, neighbouring communities, and the surrounding environment.
The objectives of this SOP are to:

Prevent and minimise emissions of VOCs, lint, dust, fine particulates, chemical vapours, and combustion gases from production and utility operations.
Monitor indoor air quality, process emissions, and ambient air quality at regular intervals and take prompt corrective action in case of deviations.
Minimise workplace and boundary-level noise generated from utilities and production machinery through engineering and administrative controls.
Control and mitigate nuisance odours arising from printing, washing, chemical storage, wastewater treatment, and waste handling activities.
Maintain full compliance with applicable environmental regulations, occupational hygiene standards, and customer environmental and social responsibility requirements relevant to the textile and apparel industry.
This SOP applies to:

All manufacturing operations involving chemical usage, printing, washing, finishing, heating, drying, ventilation, or exhaust systems.
All personnel involved in production activities, operation of fume hoods and local exhaust ventilation (LEV), chemical handling, material transfer, and waste handling.
All noise- and emission-generating equipment, including utilities (boilers, generators, compressors, chillers, cooling towers), production machinery, dust extraction systems, and exhaust stacks at RS Composite facilities.

responsibilities: Develop and implement air emission and noise monitoring programmes; assess emission risks; consolidate monitoring data; ensure compliance with statutory limits and buyer requirements; and drive corrective and preventive actions.
Enforce air-handling and ventilation protocols; ensure proper use of LEV systems and fume extraction units; and implement emission control SOPs at shop-floor level.
Maintain air pollution control equipment, exhaust systems, scrubbers, filters, silencers, and noise insulation; ensure operational uptime; and conduct calibration and preventive maintenance.
Use ventilation, dust extraction, and odour control systems correctly; follow SOPs for chemical handling; and report abnormal emissions, odours, excessive dust, or noise to supervisors and EHS.

body.text: Installed on exhausts from washing, printing, and utility operations where acidic or water-soluble vapours may be generated. Scrubbers are designed to neutralise odorous compounds and chemical vapours. Scrubber performance is verified through routine monitoring of pH, conductivity, and total dissolved solids (TDS) of recirculating scrubbing liquor.

Printing chemical preparation, mixing, and transfer activities are carried out in enclosed or semi-enclosed systems wherever feasible. Containers are kept sealed, and vapours are routed to exhaust and treatment systems to minimise fugitive emissions.

LEV systems are installed at high-risk points such as printing tables, washing machines, chemical dosing areas, and maintenance workstations. These systems capture vapours, lint, and dust at source and discharge them through filtration or scrubbing units.

Activated carbon–based adsorption units are deployed in selected high-VOC areas such as chemical storage rooms and solvent-handling zones. Carbon media is monitored for breakthrough and replaced or regenerated as per defined schedules.

Routine inspections are conducted to identify leaks from pipelines, valves, pumps, chemical containers, and exhaust ducts. Detected leaks or abnormal odours are logged, investigated, and rectified within defined corrective action timelines.

Emissions from boilers, generators, and thermic fluid heaters are controlled through proper burner design, fuel quality control, optimised combustion settings, and regular tuning to minimise NOx, SOx, CO, and particulate emissions.

Utility and process stacks are designed in accordance with regulatory guidelines for height and exit velocity to ensure effective dispersion. Sampling ports and safe access platforms are provided for stack emission monitoring.

Where applicable, continuous or periodic monitoring is carried out for parameters such as particulate matter, SOx, NOx, CO, and VOCs. Alert thresholds trigger immediate investigation and corrective action if values approach permissible limits.

steps.heading: Preventive Maintenance of Air Pollution Control (APC) Equipment

body.text: Scrubbers, filters, fans, ducts, silencers, and chimneys are included in preventive maintenance schedules. Activities include inspection of duct integrity, filter replacement, fan balancing, demister cleaning, and verification of airflow rates.

Ambient air quality monitoring is conducted at designated upwind and downwind boundary locations to assess PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, VOCs, NOx, SOx, and other relevant parameters. Trends are reviewed periodically and benchmarked against applicable ambient air quality standards to ensure negligible off-site impact.

blocks.text: At RS Composite, particulate matter (PM) generated from textile manufacturing, fabric handling, utilities, and material movement is managed through layered engineering controls, real-time monitoring, and preventive maintenance to protect worker health, ensure regulatory compliance, and prevent off-site impacts.

steps.heading: Baghouse Dust Collectors with HEPA-Grade Filters

body.text:
Baghouse systems fitted with high-efficiency (HEPA-grade) filters are installed on particulate-generating equipment such as fabric dryers, lint extraction units, brushing machines, compactors, and material handling points where fine fibres and dust are generated.
These systems provide filtration efficiency exceeding 99.9% for fine particulates, maintaining clean work environments and controlling stack emissions.

steps.heading: Wet Scrubbing Systems with Packed Bed Columns

body.text:
Wet scrubbers are connected to exhausts from washing, finishing, and chemical preparation areas where mist, aerosols, or particulate-bound vapours may be generated.
Scrubber effectiveness is assessed through pressure drop monitoring, pH checks, conductivity/TDS trends, and visual inspections of packing media and spray distribution.

ESPs are deployed on boiler stacks and other high-temperature exhaust sources to remove sub-micron particulate matter (<1 μm).
ESP performance indicators—including inlet/outlet dust load, voltage (kV), spark rate, and plate condition—are reviewed and documented during quarterly EHS and engineering audits.

PM₁₀ and PM₂.₅ sensors are installed at critical exhaust ducts and selected ambient monitoring locations.
These sensors are integrated with alarm-linked control panels that alert operators to abnormal emission spikes, triggering immediate investigation, load reduction, or controlled shutdown actions.
All particulate control systems follow defined maintenance schedules, including:

Daily or shift-wise pulse-jet cleaning (where applicable)
Weekly filter and hopper inspections
Periodic fan, motor, damper, and duct integrity checks
Calibration of differential pressure gauges and sensors to ensure sustained capture efficiency

sections.title: OC, SO₂, NOₓ, and Heavy Metal Emission Mitigation

body.text:
Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) are installed on major stacks associated with boilers, generators, thermic fluid heaters, and key exhaust systems.
Parameters monitored include SO₂, NOₓ, CO, CO₂, particulate matter, and VOCs where applicable.

AAQMS units are installed at strategic perimeter locations to monitor PM₁₀, PM₂.₅, NOₓ, SOₓ, CO, and VOCs.
The EHS team reviews monitoring data weekly or monthly, depending on operational risk levels.

Manual stack emission testing is conducted at least quarterly by accredited third-party laboratories.
Parameters tested include SO₂, NOₓ, CO, particulate matter, and total VOCs, with results certified and retained for compliance reporting.

Emission and ambient air data are consolidated into an Environmental Data Management System.
Analytics tools evaluate trends, detect anomalies, and auto-generate alarms when values approach defined action thresholds, enabling prompt corrective measures.
VOC emissions from chemical storage, printing, washing, and maintenance activities are minimised through:

Vapour balancing and return lines
Enclosed chemical transfer systems
Activated carbon adsorption units
Optimised ventilation and exhaust capture
Operational parameters are adjusted based on monitoring data to further reduce fugitive releases.

Sulphur-emitting processes are fully enclosed using sealed reactors, ducts, and processing chambers to prevent fugitive emissions.
Exhaust air from processing units is routed through sulphur absorption and recovery equipment rather than being released directly into the atmosphere.
The closed-loop system allows sulphur vapors to be captured, neutralized, and recovered for reuse or safe disposal.
Negative pressure is maintained within enclosed areas to prevent leakage into the work environment.

Dedicated emission control equipment is installed to absorb sulphur compounds through chemical scrubbing or adsorption media.
Recovered sulphur or sulphur-containing solutions are either reused in controlled processes or managed as per approved waste handling procedures.
The system operates continuously during sulphur-related production activities to ensure uninterrupted emission control.

Standard operating procedures define start-up, operation, monitoring, and shutdown of sulphur recovery systems.
Emission control equipment performance is monitored through operational efficiency checks and process parameters.
Process optimization initiatives are implemented to reduce sulphur losses and improve recovery rates.

Preventive maintenance schedules are followed to ensure integrity of enclosures, ducts, scrubbers, and recovery units.
Regular inspections are conducted to detect leaks, corrosion, or performance degradation.
Maintenance records are maintained to demonstrate system reliability and continuous operation.

The closed-circuit design significantly reduces sulphur emissions to ambient air, improving air quality within and outside the facility.
Employee exposure to sulphur fumes is minimized through engineering controls rather than reliance on PPE alone.
Emergency response procedures are in place for any abnormal emission or system failure.

CEMS and AAQMS systems are calibrated monthly or as per OEM guidance using certified calibration gases.
Preventive maintenance is conducted by trained technicians, with calibration and service records maintained under the instrumentation management system.

Emission trends, alarms, and any exceedances are reviewed by a cross-functional environmental management team.
Root cause analyses, corrective actions, and improvement projects are tracked through a central Environmental Performance Dashboard.

Annual emission reports covering stack data, APC performance, CEMS logs, and monitoring summaries are submitted to regulatory authorities as required.
Reports include pollutant loads (PM, SOₓ, NOₓ, CO, VOCs) and implemented control measures.
Chemical and auxiliary storage areas are equipped with dedicated exhaust systems designed for adequate air changes per hour (ACH) to prevent vapour and odour buildup.
Compact biofilter units using activated media and microbial biofilms are installed near odor-prone zones such as wastewater treatment areas, chemical handling zones, and waste storage points.
Solid or gel-based neutralisers are placed at identified hotspots (only where safe and compliant) to manage localised odours.
Air curtains and pressure zoning are used at entrances to prevent cross-migration of odours between production, utility, and administrative areas.
Exhaust fans, filters, scrubbers, and biofilters are maintained as per schedule, including airflow calibration, media replacement, and performance verification.

Ambient air quality is monitored continuously or at defined intervals at facility boundaries and critical internal locations.
Third-party manual monitoring is conducted at least monthly or as required.
During high-risk periods (seasonal inversions, peak production, major shutdowns/start-ups), monitoring frequency is increased.

All monitoring data is analysed by the Environmental Monitoring Team and benchmarked against applicable national ambient air quality standards and buyer expectations.
Abnormal results trigger root cause analysis and targeted mitigation actions.

Periodic noise surveys are conducted across production floors, utilities, compressor rooms, boiler houses, cooling towers, and boundary areas.
Results are benchmarked against occupational exposure limits (e.g., 85 dB(A) over 8-hour TWA).
Noise contour maps are prepared to identify high-noise zones.

Vibration isolation for compressors, pumps, blowers, and rotating equipment
Acoustic enclosures and barriers providing 10–25 dB noise reduction
Use of acoustic panels and baffles in high-noise areas

Scheduling of noise-intensive operations to minimise worker and community impact
Zoning of utilities away from offices and sensitive areas

Provision of earplugs or earmuffs in high-noise zones
Clear signage indicating mandatory hearing protection
PPE selected for comfort and compatibility with other safety gear

Routine lubrication, balancing, and alignment
Inspection of panels, guards, and fasteners to prevent rattling and vibration

Audiometric testing for exposed employees where required
Simple reporting mechanisms for abnormal noise
Regular training on noise risks and PPE use

sops.title: Actions to Avoid Road Congestion and Minimize Transport Impacts

blocks.text:
The Company recognizes that transportation activities can contribute to road congestion, community disturbance, safety risks, and indirect greenhouse gas emissions. As part of its responsible logistics and environmental management approach, structured measures are implemented to minimize traffic impact around the Company’s premises and along key transport routes.

These actions support operational efficiency, community well-being, road safety, and environmental performance.
The objectives of this procedure are to:

Prevent traffic congestion in and around the Company’s facilities
Reduce vehicle idling, delays, and unnecessary fuel consumption
Enhance road safety for employees, contractors, and local communities
Ensure responsible logistics operations aligned with environmental and social expectations

body.text:
Dispatch and receipt of raw materials and finished goods are planned to avoid peak traffic hours, particularly during morning and evening rush periods.
Delivery schedules are coordinated with transporters to stagger vehicle arrivals and departures.
High-volume shipments are consolidated where feasible to reduce the number of vehicle movements.
Advance slot booking is followed for loading and unloading activities to prevent queueing at entry gates.

Preferred transport routes are identified based on traffic density, road conditions, and proximity to residential areas.
GPS-enabled tracking systems are used to monitor vehicle movement and dynamically adjust routes in case of congestion, roadblocks, or accidents.
Transport partners are instructed to avoid narrow residential roads and sensitive community zones wherever possible.
Entry and exit points within the facility are clearly demarcated to ensure smooth vehicle circulation.

Periodic traffic impact risk assessments are conducted to identify congestion-prone periods, routes, and operational bottlenecks.
The assessment considers:
Peak-hour traffic patterns
Seasonal demand fluctuations
Nearby schools, markets, and residential areas
Emergency access requirements
Identified risks are documented, and mitigation measures such as revised delivery windows or alternative routing are implemented.

The Company is committed to eliminating the use, generation, and environmental release of Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) across its textile manufacturing operations. POPs pose significant risks to human health and the environment due to their toxicity, persistence, bioaccumulation, and long-range environmental transport.

In alignment with the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants (22 May 2001) and applicable national environmental regulations in Bangladesh, the Company has implemented systematic measures to substitute POP-containing materials, modify operational processes, and ensure safe management and disposal of POP-related waste.

Eliminate or substitute POP-containing raw materials, chemicals, and auxiliaries
Prevent unintentional formation or release of POPs during production processes
Ensure environmentally sound handling, storage, transport, and disposal of POP-related materials and waste
Achieve compliance with international conventions, customer chemical management requirements, and sustainability standards
Reduce long-term environmental and health impacts associated with POPs

At RS Composite, energy management is a core component of environmental responsibility, climate action, and operational efficiency. As a textile and ready-made garment manufacturer, RS Composite operates energy-intensive processes including knitting, cutting, stitching, printing, washing, finishing, utilities, material handling, and administrative operations. These activities require systematic control of electricity, thermal energy, and fuel consumption to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and enhance long-term sustainability.

RS Composite actively implements structured energy management practices, equipment upgrades, process optimization, and thermal efficiency measures aligned with internationally recognized environmental and energy management principles. Energy conservation initiatives are integrated with broader environmental management systems to support low-carbon operations, cost efficiency, regulatory compliance, and resilience against energy and climate risks.

Reduce direct and indirect GHG emissions arising from production, utilities, logistics support, and administrative activities.
Improve energy efficiency across HVAC systems, boilers, compressors, lighting infrastructure, production machinery, and material handling equipment.
Explore and adopt renewable energy sources and low-carbon fuels where technically and economically feasible.
Monitor, document, and continuously improve energy performance through systematic measurement, internal reviews, and management oversight.

rows: All conventional fluorescent, metal halide, and halogen fixtures across production floors, warehouses, offices, stairways, and external areas have been replaced with high-efficiency LED lighting. Motion sensors and occupancy-based controls are installed in low-traffic and intermittent-use areas such as corridors, storage rooms, washrooms, and staircases to eliminate idle energy consumption.

Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) are installed on Air Handling Units (AHUs), exhaust fans, and ventilation systems to regulate airflow based on actual occupancy and process load. Production and office areas are maintained at optimized temperature, humidity, and air-change rates to balance worker comfort, fabric quality, and energy efficiency.

Older chillers, air conditioners, and process cooling units have been progressively replaced with energy-efficient inverter-based systems. Cooling systems for utilities, electrical rooms, and process equipment are selected based on right-sizing principles to avoid oversizing and unnecessary energy draw.

Energy-efficient exhaust fans and duct designs are deployed in printing, washing, chemical preparation, and utility areas. Timers and interlocks are used to ensure ventilation systems operate only when required.

Thermal insulation improvements have been implemented for roofs, walls, windows, ducts, and piping to minimize heat gain and loss. Reflective roofing materials, insulated cladding, and sealed doors and windows are used to reduce HVAC load and improve indoor thermal comfort.

blocks.text:
Energy-efficient production machinery, including knitting machines, washing machines, dryers, compressors, and sewing equipment, is progressively adopted to reduce specific energy consumption per garment produced.
Digitally controlled machines with programmable cycles, load sensors, and auto shut-off features are used to prevent overuse of electricity during idle or low-load conditions.
High-efficiency motors (IE3/IE4 or equivalent) are installed for pumps, fans, and compressors to reduce electrical losses.
Preventive maintenance schedules are strictly followed for compressors, motors, boilers, cooling towers, pumps, and electrical panels to minimize frictional losses, air leaks, overheating, and inefficiencies that lead to excess energy consumption.

Cleaner Fuel Use in Generators

Backup diesel generators are operated using low-sulphur diesel or approved biodiesel blends where available, reducing particulate matter, SOx emissions, and overall carbon intensity.

Electrification of Heating Processes

Gas-based burners and open-flame heating devices in selected operations have been replaced with electric hot plates, induction heaters, and closed electric heating systems to improve energy efficiency and workplace safety.

Solar-Assisted Water Heating

Hot water requirements for canteens, washrooms, and selected process needs are partially met through solar-assisted water heating systems, reducing reliance on fossil fuel-based heating.

Electric Material Handling Equipment

Battery-operated forklifts, pallet movers, and trolleys are deployed in warehouses and production support areas, replacing diesel or LPG-based equipment and reducing indoor emissions and fuel consumption.

Electric Drying and Heating Equipment

Conventional fuel-fired drying systems are replaced with programmable electric dryers equipped with temperature and time controls, improving process consistency, safety, and energy efficiency.

Heat Recovery from HVAC Systems

Heat exchangers are integrated with HVAC exhaust systems to recover thermal energy from outgoing air and pre-condition incoming fresh air, reducing additional heating or cooling demand.

Closed-Loop Cooling Systems

Closed-loop cooling circuits are used for machinery, compressors, and electrical panels, enabling reuse of cooling water and reducing both energy and water consumption.

Strategic Placement of Heat-Generating Equipment

Heat-emitting equipment such as compressors, dryers, and electrical panels are strategically located to reduce space heating requirements during cooler periods where safe and appropriate.

Compressor Waste Heat Utilization

Waste heat from air compressors is captured through heat recovery units and reused for pre-heating water for cleaning, washing, or utility applications.

Steam and Condensate Recovery

Where steam systems are used, condensate is recovered and reused for boiler feed water, floor cleaning, or process pre-heating, reducing fresh energy input.

Process Heat Integration

Residual heat from dryers and washing machines is assessed for reuse in pre-heating incoming water or air streams, improving overall thermal efficiency.

RS Composite is committed to responsible and sustainable sourcing practices that uphold environmental integrity, protect human rights, and promote ethical business conduct across all tiers of its supply chain. As a textile and ready-made garment (RMG) manufacturer, RS Composite sources a wide range of inputs including yarns and fabrics, dyes and auxiliaries, chemicals, trims and accessories, packaging materials, utilities, engineering spares, logistics services, and outsourced processing services.

Given this diverse sourcing landscape, procurement decisions directly influence environmental performance (water, energy, chemicals), worker welfare, community impacts, and long-term supply resilience. This Sustainable Sourcing Manual establishes RS Composite's expectations for ESG compliance, ethical conduct, quality consistency, environmental protection, and inclusive business relationships with suppliers and service providers.

Identify and mitigate environmental, social, and human rights risks across RS Composite's upstream supply chain, including textile raw materials, chemicals, processing services, and logistics.
Promote ethical, transparent, and inclusive sourcing practices aligned with internationally recognized principles, ISO standards, and RS Composite's internal ESG framework.
Evaluate, engage, and improve supplier performance through structured ESG assessments, audits, and capacity-building initiatives.
Strengthen supplier accountability on labor rights, non-discrimination, safe workplaces, environmental protection, and responsible chemical management.
Support long-term sustainability and resilience through responsible material sourcing, traceability, and low-impact production practices.

body.text: All suppliers—whether providing yarns, fabrics, chemicals, trims, packaging, services, or logistics—must review, sign, and comply with RS Composite's Supplier Code of Conduct, which covers:

Human rights and decent work
Ethical business conduct
Environmental performance
Safe and responsible chemical handling
Zero tolerance for corruption, bribery, harassment, or discrimination
Annual reaffirmation ensures continued commitment.
RS Composite gives preference to suppliers who:

Demonstrate environmental management systems aligned with ISO 14001 (or equivalent).
Minimize emissions, hazardous waste, chemical losses, and water pollution.
Implement energy-efficient technologies and, where feasible, renewable energy.
Follow responsible material sourcing practices, including fibre traceability, reduced environmental impact, and protection of ecosystems.
Chemical suppliers must comply with applicable chemical management standards and restricted substance requirements.
Suppliers must adhere to:

Prohibition of child labor, forced labor, and human trafficking
Fair wages meeting or exceeding local statutory requirements
Safe and healthy working conditions aligned with ISO 45001 principles
Equal opportunity, diversity, and non-discrimination
Freedom of association and effective grievance mechanisms
Worker welfare is a mandatory audit criterion.
RS Composite promotes inclusive sourcing by encouraging business with:

Women-owned enterprises
Small and medium enterprises (SMEs/MSMEs)
Minority-owned or socially disadvantaged businesses
Supplier diversity information is collected during onboarding and tracked as a sustainability indicator.
Procurement decisions follow a zero-tolerance approach to:

Corruption, bribery, and facilitation payments
Conflicts of interest
Unfair vendor favoritism
All sourcing decisions must be transparent, documented, and traceable.

RS Composite is committed to ensuring that all customers, buyers, brands, and downstream users can safely handle, process, wear, and use the textile and garment products manufactured and supplied by the company. As a manufacturer of textile fabrics, knitwear, and ready-made garments, RS Composite supplies products that ultimately reach global consumers, including children, workers, and sensitive user groups.

Although RS Composite does not manufacture chemical products for direct consumer sale, its operations involve dyes, auxiliaries, finishing chemicals, fabrics, trims, and packaging materials that can pose health and safety risks if not properly controlled. Therefore, RS Composite takes full responsibility for identifying potential customer health and safety risks, controlling them at source, and communicating relevant information transparently throughout the product lifecycle.

This SOP defines the systems and controls adopted to protect customer health and safety from material selection and chemical management to labeling, documentation, restricted substance compliance, recall readiness, and buyer communication.

Ensure that all customers and downstream users receive accurate, complete, and timely health and safety information related to RS Composite’s textile and garment products.
Establish structured systems for hazard identification, chemical risk assessment, and health impact evaluation across fabrics, dyes, finishes, accessories, and packaging.
Maintain transparent disclosure regarding chemical use, restricted substances, allergenic risks, finishing treatments, and safe use instructions.
Proactively assess risks related to new materials, innovative finishes, performance coatings, and functional textiles.
Ensure compliance with applicable global and buyer-specific standards, including GHS, ZDHC MRSL, REACH, CPSIA, OEKO-TEX®, and ISO-aligned management systems.

Defined storage conditions for finished goods to prevent chemical migration, odor formation, or degradation.
