RS Composite is committed to maintaining a fair, transparent, and ethical recruitment process that attracts competent talent while fully respecting human rights, labor laws, and equal opportunity principles. As a company operating in the textile and garment manufacturing industry, RS Composite recognizes that responsible recruitment is fundamental to building a diverse, skilled, and compliant workforce across production units, offices, and support functions.

This Recruitment Procedure SOP establishes a structured framework to ensure that all hiring activities are conducted objectively, without discrimination, and in strict compliance with applicable labor laws. Particular emphasis is placed on equal opportunity during hiring, non-discrimination, and robust age verification measures to prevent underage employment across all operations and employment categories.
The objectives of this Recruitment Procedure SOP are to:

Ensure a fair, merit-based, and transparent recruitment process for all roles at RS Composite.
Promote equal opportunity and prevent discrimination during hiring, selection, and onboarding.
Prevent child labor and underage employment through systematic age verification and legal compliance.
Ensure recruitment practices align with national labor laws, buyer codes of conduct, and international standards such as ILO Conventions.
Maintain proper documentation, traceability, and accountability throughout the recruitment lifecycle.
This SOP applies to:

All recruitment activities undertaken by RS Composite for permanent, temporary, contract, apprentice, and trainee positions.
All departments, including production, quality, maintenance, administration, HR, merchandising, and management functions.
All hiring locations, including factories, offices, and third-party labor sourcing arrangements.
All personnel involved in recruitment, including HR staff, department heads, supervisors, and authorized recruitment agents.

sections.title: Equal Opportunity and Non-Discrimination During Hiring

blocks.text: RS Composite is an equal opportunity employer and strictly prohibits discrimination at any stage of recruitment.

sections.title: Equal Opportunity and Non-Discrimination During Hiring

body.text:
All recruitment decisions are based solely on job-related criteria such as skills, experience, qualifications, and suitability for the role.
No applicant shall be discriminated against on the basis of:
Gender or gender identity
Age (above legal minimum)
Religion, caste, ethnicity, or nationality
Disability or health condition (unless job-critical and legally justified)
Marital status, pregnancy, or family responsibilities
Job advertisements and vacancy notices use neutral and inclusive language.

Screening criteria are standardized and documented prior to candidate evaluation.
Interview questions focus strictly on professional competence and role requirements.
Personal questions unrelated to job performance (e.g., family planning, religion, political beliefs) are strictly prohibited.
Interview panels are trained on unconscious bias and ethical recruitment practices.

Women candidates are encouraged to apply for both operational and supervisory roles.
Reasonable accommodations are provided to candidates with disabilities during interviews where feasible.
Migrant and local workers are treated equally in hiring, wages, and employment conditions.

sections.title: Age Verification and Prevention of Underage Employment

blocks.text: RS Composite maintains zero tolerance for child labor and strictly enforces age verification prior to employment.

sections.title: Age Verification and Prevention of Underage Employment

body.text:
The minimum age for employment is strictly in line with applicable national labor laws and factory regulations.
No person below the legally permitted working age is allowed to work at any RS Composite facility, directly or indirectly.
Before final selection and onboarding, HR must verify at least one valid government-issued proof of age, such as:

Birth Certificate
Aadhaar Card
School Leaving Certificate
Passport
Any other legally recognized age proof

Original documents are physically checked by HR personnel.
Copies of verified documents are retained in the employee personal file.
Date of birth is recorded in the HR management system and cross-verified during audits.
In case of doubt regarding age authenticity, employment is withheld until clarification or independent verification is completed.

Recruitment agents and contractors are contractually obligated to comply with age verification requirements.
Random age verification checks are conducted during internal audits and buyer inspections.
Supervisors are trained to report any suspected underage employment immediately to HR and Compliance teams.

If any underage worker is identified, immediate removal from work is ensured without penalty to the individual.
A remediation plan is initiated, which may include support for education or vocational training, as per legal and ethical guidelines.
Root cause analysis is conducted, and corrective actions are implemented to prevent recurrence.

Final selection is approved jointly by HR and the concerned Department Head.
Offer letters clearly define role, wages, working hours, benefits, and employment terms.
No recruitment fees are charged to candidates at any stage.
All employees undergo induction covering company policies, code of conduct, health & safety, and labor rights.

sops.title: Employee Performance Evaluation and Career Progression Framework

blocks.text:
RS Composite recognizes that its employees are the key drivers of operational excellence, product quality, compliance, and customer satisfaction within the textile and garment manufacturing industry. Consistent performance in areas such as knitting, stitching, finishing, quality control, production planning, compliance, health & safety, and supply chain management depends on a motivated, skilled, and continuously developing workforce.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes a structured framework for evaluating employee performance and enabling systematic career progression across all functions of RS Composite, including Production, Quality, Maintenance, EHS, HR, Compliance, Merchandising, Supply Chain, Administration, and Management functions.
The framework is designed to ensure objective, transparent, consistent, and development-oriented performance evaluations that support individual growth while strengthening organizational capability, buyer compliance, and long-term sustainability.
The Employee Performance Evaluation & Career Progression Framework at RS Composite aims to:

Ensure Fair and Consistent Reviews: Apply a standardized and evidence-based appraisal process across all departments and job levels.
Support Employee Development: Align individual career aspirations with organizational objectives through clearly defined growth pathways.
Use Comprehensive Performance Indicators: Combine productivity metrics, quality outcomes, compliance behavior, teamwork, and behavioral competencies for a balanced performance view.
Encourage a Feedback-Driven Culture: Promote open communication, regular coaching, and constructive feedback.
Ensure Legal and Policy Alignment: Adhere to internal HR policies, labor laws, equal opportunity commitments, and buyer code of conduct requirements.
Enable Data-Informed Talent Decisions: Maintain structured documentation to support promotions, training needs, succession planning, and workforce stability.
This SOP applies to all permanent, contractual, probationary, and supervisory employees across all RS Composite factories, offices, and operational locations. It covers:

Quarterly, half-yearly, and annual performance appraisals
Goal setting and KPI definition
Performance monitoring and documentation
Individual Development Plans (IDPs)
Technical, operational, behavioral, and leadership competency evaluation
Training, upskilling, and cross-functional exposure
Career progression, promotions, and internal mobility

Suggestion Box & Confidential Feedback: Employees may raise concerns, suggestions, or improvement ideas anonymously.

Ratings and recommendations are reviewed and acknowledged by:

Employee
Supervisor

HR
High-performing employees may be considered for:

Skill enhancement
Role expansion

Succession planning pipelines

Periodic follow-ups to monitor progress

Incorporate employee and supervisor feedback

Strengthen transparency, consistency, and engagement
Employee surveys, HR analytics, and audit findings are used to enhance effectiveness.
RS Composite ensures that all performance evaluations are conducted with confidentiality, respect, and impartiality. The company is committed to:

Equal opportunity for all employees regardless of gender, caste, religion, ethnicity, age, or background
Compliance with labor laws, social compliance standards, and internal HR policies
Regular internal reviews to identify and address bias, documentation gaps, or process deviations
Employees may raise appraisal-related grievances with HR. Unresolved cases are reviewed by a neutral committee to ensure fair resolution.
Each grievance case is documented with:

Nature of concern

Access to grievance records is restricted to HR and authorized management personnel.
RS Composite continuously strengthens its people management practices by:

Reviewing this SOP periodically
Integrating performance and compliance indicators into internal audits
Collecting employee feedback through surveys and forums
Benchmarking against industry best practices
Updating procedures in response to regulatory, buyer, and operational changes
Insights from these efforts reinforce a workplace culture built on fairness, growth, accountability, and long-term employee development.

The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to establish clear, enforceable, and comprehensive procedures to prevent any form of excessive use of force, harassment, intimidation, coercion, or obstruction of employee movement by security personnel at RS Composite.

This SOP ensures that all security-related interactions strictly uphold human dignity, fundamental human rights, and respect for individuals, while complying with applicable labour laws, criminal laws, buyer codes of conduct, and internationally accepted principles such as the UN Basic Principles on the Use of Force and Conduct of Law Enforcement Officials.
This SOP reinforces RS Composite's commitment to:

Safeguarding the physical, emotional, and psychological well-being of all employees and individuals on site
Preventing fear, coercion, humiliation, or undue stress in the workplace
Ensuring security personnel function as protectors of safety and assets, not as enforcers of discipline
Establishing a clear, transparent reporting, investigation, and accountability framework
This SOP applies to:

All in-house security guards deployed at RS Composite locations
All third-party security agency personnel engaged under contract
Security supervisors, shift-in-charges, and site security leads
HR, Administration, and Compliance teams responsible for oversight
All operations at factories, offices, warehouses, production units, and transport gates

This SOP applies to all individuals present on RS Composite premises, including permanent employees, contract workers, trainees, apprentices, interns, visitors, vendors, service providers, and logistics personnel.

rows.definition:
Any physical, verbal, or psychological action beyond what is strictly necessary to address an immediate safety threat. This includes, but is not limited to:
Pushing, grabbing, twisting arms, or restraining
Forcing individuals to sit, stand, or remain in one place against their will
Blocking exits or detaining individuals
Shouting, threatening, or intimidating language
Humiliation, body shaming, or aggressive posturing
The right of individuals to enter, exit, and move freely within the workplace without obstruction, except where temporary restrictions are lawfully required for safety, security, or legal reasons.
The minimum level of force required solely to protect life or prevent serious harm. It never includes punitive, retaliatory, or disciplinary actions.
Any act of holding, confining, or preventing a person from leaving company premises without lawful authority.
Any form of pressure, intimidation, manipulation, or threat used to influence an individual's actions or decisions.

responsibilities: Ensure strict implementation of this SOP across all shifts and posts.

Maintain records of training, audits, complaints, and investigations.
Investigate complaints confidentially, impartially, and objectively.
Recommend corrective, disciplinary, or contractual actions as required.
Manage and periodically evaluate third-party security agency performance.
Ensure adequate CCTV coverage at gates, access points, and critical areas.
Coordinate with HR and Compliance to ensure timely corrective actions.
Treat all individuals with dignity, respect, and professionalism.
Follow this SOP and supervisor instructions without deviation.
Use de-escalation techniques to manage conflicts.
Never use force unless there is an immediate threat to safety.
Promptly report incidents, unsafe situations, or deviations.

body.text: Security personnel must never engage in the following:

Physical actions such as pushing, dragging, restraining, twisting, or blocking movement
Raising voice, shouting, threatening, or intimidating behaviour
Abusive, discriminatory, or derogatory language
Unnecessary or inappropriate physical contact
Confiscation of personal belongings, documents, tools, or mobile phones
Intentional delays at gates without valid justification
Acting as disciplinarians or enforcing HR-related matters
Forcing employees to stand in lines or wait excessively
Preventing exit during emergencies or medical situations
Demanding bribes, favours, or personal benefits
Any such act is treated as a serious human rights violation.

steps.heading: Conditions for Permitted Use of Force

body.text: Use of force is permitted only when all the following conditions are met:

There is an immediate threat to life or serious physical harm.
All lesser measures (verbal instruction, distancing, de-escalation) have failed.
The force used is minimal, proportionate, and stops once the threat is neutralized.
Medical assistance is arranged immediately if injury occurs.
The incident is reported without delay and fully documented.
Force must never be used to discipline, punish, restrict movement, or assert authority.
Security personnel must:

Speak politely in a calm, respectful tone
Maintain non-threatening body language
Ask questions courteously, not interrogate
Avoid gestures that may create fear or discomfort
Maintain confidentiality of employee interactions
Respect cultural sensitivities and diversity
All communication must be clear, professional, neutral, and non-judgmental.
Security must allow employees to:

Enter and exit freely at scheduled shift times
Leave during emergencies, medical needs, or personal crises
Access authorized work areas without unjustified restrictions
Move freely within the premises as per operational permissions
Strictly Prohibited:

Blocking gates during shift changes
Preventing exit during labour issues or disputes
Confiscating gate passes
Locking exits without authorization
Group detainment for "checking"
Movement restrictions may only be authorised by HR/Admin during:

Emergency lockdowns
Verified security breaches
Legally mandated investigations

Effective internal communication is critical to ensuring operational alignment, production efficiency, worker safety, compliance with buyer requirements, and ethical workplace practices across all units of RS Composite. As a garment and textile manufacturing organization involved in knitting, stitching, finishing, washing, quality control, packing, warehousing, and administrative operations, RS Composite relies on clear, timely, and structured communication to support productivity, quality consistency, regulatory compliance, and employee engagement.

Given the multi-shift, labour-intensive, and compliance-driven nature of the apparel industry, accurate dissemination of information related to production planning, quality standards, health & safety, audits, and employee welfare is essential. This SOP establishes a formal internal communication framework to ensure transparency, coordination, accountability, and continuous improvement across all departments and levels.

sops.title: Emergency Preparedness & Response for Environment, Health & Safety (EHS)

blocks.text: The objective of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to establish and maintain a structured Emergency Preparedness & Response system at RS Composite that identifies all foreseeable environmental, health, and safety emergencies; defines preventive, control, and mitigation measures; and ensures a coordinated, timely, and effective response during any emergency situation.

This procedure ensures that emergency controls are periodically tested, evaluated, and revised in line with RS Composite's commitments under ISO 14001 (Environmental Management), ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety), buyer social compliance requirements, and internal EHS management standards.
This SOP applies to any emergency situation that may pose a risk to employee health, safety, company assets, surrounding communities, or the environment across RS Composite's facilities, including:

Garment manufacturing units (cutting, stitching, finishing, packing)
Washing, processing, and utility areas
Warehouses and material storage areas
R&D / sampling / quality inspection sections
Administrative offices, canteens, and common facilities
The scope includes, but is not limited to:

Fire and explosion incidents
Electrical failures and shocks
Chemical spills (cleaning agents, solvents, fuels, oils)
Occupational injuries and accidents
Natural disasters (earthquake, flood, storm, extreme weather)
Utility failures (power, water, compressed air)

responsibilities: Implement this Emergency Preparedness & Response SOP across all sites, ensure readiness, communication, coordination, training, mock drills, and periodic reviews.

Identification of Emergency Scenarios

Main security gates

Offices and control rooms

Fire brigade

Contact information is reviewed and updated periodically.

Activation of Emergency

Upon confirmation of a major emergency:
The Security Officer / Security Guard activates the emergency siren upon instruction from the Site Emergency Controller.

Emergency Siren Pattern

- Emergency Alert (Wailing Siren): 30 seconds ON, 10 seconds OFF, repeated for 2 minutes
- All-Clear Siren: Continuous sound for 2 minutes

Weekly Siren Testing

- Conducted once every week at a fixed time
- HR / EHS informs all department heads in advance
- No evacuation is required during siren testing

RS Composite maintains a documented Onsite Emergency Plan prepared by the Management Representative and Department Heads, covering:

Emergency organization structure
Roles and responsibilities
Evacuation routes and emergency exits
Assembly points
Firefighting and first-aid resources
Chemical hazards and environmental risks
Communication and coordination mechanisms

Environmental impacts and occupational health & safety hazards are integral to emergency risk assessment and response planning.

Fire incidents
Electrical shocks and panel fires
Flooding during heavy rains
Earthquakes
Falling from height
Chemical leaks or spills
Storage area emergencies
Utility system failures

Emergency Helpline Numbers

External Emergency Services
Internal Key Personnel – RS Composite

Fire Emergency

Prevention

Maintain fire extinguishers, hydrants, alarms, and detectors in working condition.
Conduct routine inspections and housekeeping.
Train employees and security staff in fire extinguisher usage.
Ensure proper storage of flammable materials.
Mitigation

Inform Security and Supervisor immediately.
Use appropriate extinguishers (electrical, fabric, oil-based fires).
Evacuate through staircases; do not use lifts.
Move to designated assembly points.
Isolate affected area and disconnect power if safe.
Call Fire Brigade if fire is uncontrollable.
Assess and address environmental impact post-incident.

Electrical Shock / Short Circuit

Prevention

Mandatory PPE for electrical work.
Rubber mats at all electrical panels.
Clear "Danger – High Voltage" signage.
Proper earthing and protective devices (MCB, ELCB).
Only authorized electricians allowed to work on electrical systems.
Mitigation

Switch off power immediately.
Separate the victim safely from the power source.
Provide first aid by trained personnel.
Shift to medical facility if required.

Earthquake

Mitigation

Evacuate calmly through emergency exits to open assembly areas.
Do not use elevators.
Assist employees unfamiliar with procedures.

Thunderstorm / Heavy Rain / Dust Storm

Mitigation

Move indoors and away from open areas.
Secure doors, windows, and loose materials.
Avoid contact with electrical wiring.

Occupational Accidents

Includes slips, trips, falls, needle injuries, electrical shocks, and machine-related injuries.

Immediate first aid provided.
Incident reported to EHS and HR.
Mock drills conducted periodically.
Emergency maps and siren codes displayed at key locations.

Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA)

For all emergency incidents:

Root cause analysis is conducted.
Corrective and preventive actions are documented.
Regulatory notifications are made where required.
Lessons learned are communicated to employees.
Review and Disposition

The Onsite Emergency Plan is reviewed at least once every three years or earlier if required due to process changes, incidents, or regulatory updates.
Mock drills are conducted periodically and findings documented.
All revisions are recorded and retained.

RS Composite is committed to maintaining the highest standards of information security, data privacy, operational continuity, and ethical business conduct across all its manufacturing, administrative, and supply-chain operations. As a garment and textile manufacturing organization serving international buyers, brands, and compliance-driven markets, the protection of confidential business information, employee data, buyer specifications, and operational systems is essential for maintaining trust, regulatory compliance, and uninterrupted production.

This Incident Response Procedure (IRP) establishes a structured, timely, and traceable approach for identifying, reporting, containing, investigating, and resolving information security, data privacy, and operational system incidents. The procedure safeguards sensitive information, digital infrastructure, physical records, and internal systems from unauthorized access, misuse, loss, or disruption.
The primary objectives of this procedure are to:

Protect confidential and sensitive information, including employee personal data, payroll records, buyer specifications, production plans, costing data, quality reports, and compliance documentation.
Ensure rapid detection, containment, and mitigation of information security incidents or data breaches.
Minimize operational disruption, production delays, and reputational risks.
Conduct structured investigations and risk assessments to prevent recurrence.
Enable clear, controlled, and accurate communication during any incident.
Ensure compliance with applicable labour laws, buyer data-protection requirements, and contractual confidentiality obligations.
Preserve stakeholder confidence among buyers, auditors, regulators, suppliers, and employees.
This SOP applies to all:

Permanent employees
Contract and temporary workers
Interns and apprentices
Consultants and service providers
Third-party vendors with system, data, or site access
It covers incidents involving:

Digital systems (ERP, payroll systems, attendance systems, production planning software, email, shared drives)
Physical records (personnel files, audit reports, contracts, production records)
Portable devices (USB drives, laptops, tablets, external hard drives)
Cloud-based storage and collaboration platforms
Network infrastructure and CCTV systems
Any medium used to store or process confidential information
This procedure applies during working hours, off-hours, remote work, field operations, audits, and emergency situations.

body.text: Any employee who discovers or suspects an incident must act immediately. Treat All Incidents as High Priority. Unusual system behavior, missing files, unauthorized access alerts, suspicious emails, data leakage, or physical document loss must never be ignored.

substeps.text: Contain the Incident (If Safe to Do So): Disconnect affected systems from the network. Log out of compromised user accounts. Stop active data transfers or unauthorized access. Remove external storage devices involved.

Notify the Incident Response Team (IRT) Immediately: Incidents must be reported through any available internal channel: Designated incident reporting email; IT / Compliance contact number; Internal reporting form or ERP alert; Direct phone or WhatsApp message to IT, HR, or Compliance.

Document Critical Details: The reporter must record: Date and time of discovery; Location (office, factory floor, server, system, file cabinet, etc.); Systems or documents affected; Actions already taken; Visible or suspected impact.
Preserve Evidence: Do not delete files, logs, emails, or CCTV footage. Do not reset devices unless instructed. Do not attempt independent fixes or data recovery.

body.text: Severity Assessment: Incidents are classified as: High Severity: Data breach involving employee data, buyer information, payroll, cyberattack, ransomware, system sabotage, theft of records. Medium Severity: Malware detection, unauthorized internal access, compromised credentials. Low Severity: Accidental email misdelivery, policy deviations, near-miss events.

substeps.text: Containment Measures: Disable affected user accounts. Block unauthorized network access. Isolate affected devices or systems. Secure physical locations or document storage.
Evidence Collection: System and access logs; Email trails and screenshots; ERP audit trails; CCTV footage (for physical incidents).
Internal Notifications: Inform relevant stakeholders: HR; IT; Compliance; Department Heads; Senior Management.

Escalation (If Required): Engage: External IT security or forensic experts; Legal advisors; Law enforcement (for theft, sabotage, or criminal acts); Buyer-mandated reporting channels where contractually required.

body.text: Internal Communication: Employees are informed strictly on a need-to-know basis. Instructions are issued to prevent further risk. Confidentiality is reinforced to avoid rumors or misinformation. External Communication: Used only if buyer, supplier, or third-party data is affected. Communication includes: Brief incident description; Immediate containment actions; Required actions by the stakeholder (if any); Designated contact person. Media & Public Communication: Handled exclusively by: Managing Director / CEO; Authorized Senior Management Representative. Unauthorized disclosure is strictly prohibited.

The Compliance and Legal teams will: Assess Legal and Contractual Obligations including: National data protection and labour laws; Buyer codes of conduct and confidentiality clauses; Audit and disclosure requirements. Prepare Notifications (If required) within defined timelines, covering: Nature of the incident; Data or systems impacted; Mitigation actions taken; Preventive steps planned. Maintain Documentation: All incident records are retained for audits, buyer reviews, and legal reference.

blocks.text: After incident resolution:

Post-Incident Review: Evaluate: Root cause; Detection and response gaps; Communication effectiveness; System or procedural weaknesses.
Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA): May include: System upgrades; Stronger access controls; Password and MFA enforcement; SOP revisions; Process redesign.
Training & Awareness: Refresher training for employees; Phishing and data-handling awareness; Controlled sharing of lessons learned.
Incident Simulations: Conducted annually or semi-annually: Cyber-incident drills; Data-loss simulations; Mock breach response exercises.
Annual Review of IRP: This procedure is reviewed annually or upon: Major incidents; Regulatory updates; Buyer requirement changes; Technology upgrades.

RSIs may occur during activities such as sewing, cutting, ironing, finishing, packing, material handling, quality inspection, machine operation, embroidery, printing, and administrative or computer-based work.

Reduce physical strain and prevent discomfort, fatigue, or injury caused by repetitive work and poor posture.
Improve productivity, comfort, and worker well-being through proactive ergonomic controls.

A structured evaluation of tasks, tools, workstation design, and worker posture to identify risk factors that may lead to musculoskeletal disorders.
Short, frequent breaks (typically 30–60 seconds) taken during repetitive work to reduce muscle fatigue and cumulative strain.

responsibilities: Conduct ergonomic risk assessments for high-risk tasks and workstations.
Recommend engineering, administrative, and procedural controls (chairs, tables, lighting, tool redesign, workstation adjustments).
Provide ergonomic awareness and RSI prevention training.
Maintain records of assessments, corrective actions, and reviews.

Ensure ergonomic guidelines are followed on the shop floor.
Implement job rotation, work-rest cycles, and task variation.
Integrate ergonomic awareness into induction and refresher training programs.
Monitor trends related to musculoskeletal complaints or medical records.

body.text: Tasks involving repetitive motion, force, vibration, prolonged standing/sitting, awkward posture, or precision handling are identified and listed.
The EHS team evaluates:

Worker posture and movement
Height and layout of tables, sewing machines, cutting benches, and ironing stations
Reach distance and material placement
Chair, stool, and footrest suitability
Lighting levels and glare
Frequency and duration of repetitive movements
Tasks are classified as Low, Medium, or High Risk based on ergonomic risk criteria.
Improvements may include:

Adjustable chairs, stools, or worktables
Anti-fatigue mats for standing work
Modified or lighter hand tools
Job rotation schedules
Mechanical aids for lifting or material transfer
Reduction of repetitive cycle time or exposure
High-risk tasks are re-assessed at least once every six months or after any significant process change.

Adjustable sewing tables and cutting tables
Chairs with lumbar support for machine operators
Footrests for seated workstations
Anti-fatigue mats for standing operations
Proper workstation height alignment to reduce bending and shoulder strain

Lightweight scissors, tools, and attachments
Ergonomically designed handles and grips
Vibration-reduced machinery where applicable
Use of trolleys, conveyors, and lifting aids to reduce manual handling

Rotation between high-repetition and low-strain tasks
Defined work-rest schedules
Mandatory microbreaks during continuous or repetitive operations
Training covers:

Proper sitting and standing posture
Correct lifting and handling techniques
Hand, wrist, shoulder, and back exercises
Early signs and symptoms of RSI
Importance of workstation adjustment
Training is conducted during induction and at least quarterly thereafter.

narrative.text:

Periodic occupational health check-ups include musculoskeletal screening for high-risk roles.

The workstation or task is reviewed for ergonomic deficiencies.
Corrective actions are implemented (redesign, rotation, training).

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes a structured, transparent, and effective process for collecting, documenting, evaluating, and resolving customer feedback related to product quality, compliance, environmental aspects, delivery performance, or health and safety concerns.
The objective of this system is to ensure that customer feedback is addressed promptly, consistently, and professionally, enabling RS Composite to:

Strengthen customer satisfaction and long-term trust
Drive continuous improvement across operations
Maintain compliance with applicable national and international standards
Meet buyer expectations under ISO 9001 (Quality Management Systems) and global customer audit requirements
This SOP applies to:

All customer interactions, both domestic and international
Buyers, brand customers, buying houses, agents, and supply-chain partners
Feedback received through any formal or informal communication channel
The SOP covers the complete feedback lifecycle, including:

Feedback collection
Evaluation and categorization
Escalation of critical issues
Investigation and root-cause analysis
Corrective and preventive action (CAPA)
Documentation, communication, and management review

rows.definition: Any comment, complaint, suggestion, inquiry, or observation related to RS Composite’s products, workmanship, packaging, documentation, delivery timelines, safety, environmental performance, or compliance requirements.
Feedback involving serious product non-conformance, safety risk, regulatory breach, shipment rejection, or significant customer impact.
Feedback affecting service levels, documentation accuracy, delivery coordination, or minor quality deviations that do not pose safety or regulatory risk.
Suggestions, compliments, or minor service-related inputs with no direct impact on quality, safety, or compliance.

body.text: RS Composite provides multiple channels for customers to share feedback, including:

Customer feedback received through any approved channel is immediately forwarded to the Customer Service, Merchandising, or Quality team.

RS Composite is committed to conducting all third-party relationships with integrity, transparency, fairness, and accountability. As a manufacturer operating within the composites and advanced materials industry—covering fiberglass, resin systems, engineered components, tooling, logistics, and technical services—RS Composite recognizes that third-party conduct directly impacts legal compliance, human rights, environmental performance, and business reputation.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) establishes a structured framework to ensure that suppliers, contractors, service providers, logistics partners, consultants, and outsourced service providers comply with RS Composite’s ethical, legal, labor, environmental, health & safety, and data security expectations.
This procedure supports responsible sourcing, ethical procurement, regulatory compliance, and sustainable value-chain performance.
This SOP is designed to ensure:

Ethical and compliant onboarding of all third-party partners
Identification and mitigation of risks such as bribery, fraud, labor exploitation, unsafe working conditions, environmental violations, or data misuse
Assurance of fair labor practices, safe workplaces, and respect for human rights
Alignment with applicable environmental regulations, ISO standards, and RS Composite’s sustainability commitments
Verification of confidentiality, data privacy, and cybersecurity practices
Transparent documentation, traceability, and audit readiness
Ongoing monitoring, audits, corrective actions, and incident reporting for sustained compliance
This SOP applies to all departments engaging third parties for:

Raw materials and composite inputs (fibers, resins, additives, core materials)
Manufacturing support and fabrication services
Tooling, machining, and engineering services
Logistics, transportation, and warehousing
Facility management, maintenance, and utilities
IT services, data processing, and professional consulting
Project-based contractors and outsourced operations
The procedure applies across all RS Composite locations, projects, and business operations.

substeps.text: Integrity & Anti-Corruption: Review history of bribery, fraud, litigation, or unethical conduct; Confirm commitment to applicable anti-corruption laws and ethical business practices

Environmental Responsibility: Review environmental permits, waste management practices, and compliance history; Evaluate pollution prevention measures, emissions control, and resource efficiency; Verify certifications such as ISO 14001
Information Security & Data Protection: Review data security policies and confidentiality controls; Ensure protection of drawings, designs, customer data, and proprietary information
Occupational Health & Safety: Verify safety training, PPE usage, incident records, and emergency preparedness; Assess compliance with applicable OHS standards and safe-work practices
